Mineral Resources
No mineral resources of economic value except coal are known to be present on Tracts II and III within the depths that will be disturbed by the proposed mining activity. Oil and gas may be present at great depths beneath the Tracts, but mining and reclamation activities associated with coal extraction would not preclude the exploration for and development of these resources. Thus, the short-term use of Tracts II and III for strip mining of low sulfur coal would have no effect on the long-term productivity of other mineral resources of economic value that may be present beneath the Tracts.
Water Resources
The use of Tracts II and III for strip mining of coal will have both short and long-term effects on the water resources of the area. These effects should be localized with respect to long-term productivity as the 25,000 acres to be mined represents less than 5% of the total drainage area of Tullock, Sarpy and East Fork of Sarpy Creek.
Losses of the shallow aquifers in approximately 25,000 acres of lands to be mined in Tracts II and III will be permanent. Runoff rates from the mined areas may reflect changed water infiltration characteristics caused by the disturbed and intermixed overburden. The movement of precipitation through the reclaimed spoils will result in the leaching and transport of dissolved solids, including sulfates, carbonates and alkaline earth metals. It is not known whether the replaced spoils would function as a suitable source of ground-water supply for livestock and domestic use after mining ceases, although suitable water supplies will be available from deeper aquifers in the Fort Union Formation.
